newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: BOURSE BLOCK TRADE COMMISSION CEILING OKAYED.
newsitem.headline: BOURSE BLOCK TRADE COMMISSION CEILING OKAYED.

text.p: Lithuania's securities commission said on Saturday that it had okayed a bourse request to impose a 15,000 litas ceiling on the exchange's commission for portfolio block trades.

Buyers and sellers are currently charged a 0.25 percent commission by the bourse for most block portfolio transactions - deals involving ten percent or more of a company's shares - and 0.15 percent for trades of shares on the official list.
Those rules remain in force, but the limit charged by the bourse will now be 15,000 litas, regardless of the size of the deal, an official with the securities commission told Reuters.
Dealers, who lobbied hard for the move in an effort to stimulate activity on the sluggish bourse, welcomed the changes.
"This should increase trade, especially big block deals," one broker told Reuters.
